input.quote: 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: The grant in §§ 13.1–13.3 meets the preferred position: it names Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf (no notice or consent gate); paid-up software and embedded Vendor Technology are licensed perpetually, irrevocably, royalty-free with modification and contractor-support rights (§ 13.2); the subscription licence may be revoked or suspended only for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity (§ 13.3); and licence rights are transferable to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a § 24-permitted assignment, which § 24.1 allows without Vendor consent for mergers and asset sales. Nothing is revocable at Vendor's discretion. The only tension is § 14.2's "revocable, non-transferable" Deliverable licence limited to the Order Form term, but § 14.3 pulls the § 13.2 perpetual licence into Deliverables containing Vendor Technology; that Deliverable ownership/revocability point belongs to the IP rule and is not flagged again here.
